problem: LLM pruning methods are widely used for efficiency but remain unexplored for security vulnerabilities.
approach: The paper introduces an attack where an adversary computes a proxy metric for pruning likelihood and injects malicious behaviors into unprunable parameters while using prunable parameters to mask them during pre-pruning.
contribution: Demonstrates that modern pruning methods can be maliciously exploited with success rates up to 95.7% for jailbreak and 99.5% for targeted injection, revealing a critical deployment-time security gap.

problem: Attention in transformer prefill is computationally expensive due to processing all key-value pairs, slowing inference.
approach: QuoKA leverages query-key similarity patterns to prioritize low-similarity queries and retain representative queries, then selects aligned key-value pairs for sparse attention evaluation.
contribution: Achieves 3x reduction in time-to-first-token and up to 7x speedup on Intel CPUs while utilizing 88% fewer key-value pairs and maintaining near-baseline accuracy.

problem: Multi-view clustering fails on incomplete data where some views are missing, and existing recovery methods introduce errors.
approach: The method proposes confident block diagonal structures to infer missing views while preserving invariable local structure, combined with graph completion across all views.
contribution: Demonstrates superior performance on multiple benchmark datasets compared to state-of-the-art incomplete multi-view clustering methods.

problem: Differentiable physics simulators produce erratic or vanishing gradients in contact-rich tasks, hindering optimization.
approach: A differentiable contact model is proposed that satisfies well-behaved gradient properties while maintaining computational efficiency in rigid-body simulation.
contribution: Enables discovery of complex contact-rich control signals from simple initializations for locomotion and manipulation tasks.

problem: Multimodal LLMs process excessive visual tokens, increasing computational cost without improving task performance.
approach: The method uses explainability techniques (attention maps) to identify task-irrelevant visual tokens at the input stage of LLMs, trained via lightweight convolutional networks.
contribution: Achieves significant token reduction with negligible performance loss across 13 benchmarks on three leading MLLMs without architecture modification.

problem: Video restoration using generative models suffers from distribution drift and poor texture quality due to imperfect alignment.
approach: Vivid-VR combines concept distillation from a pretrained T2V model with a redesigned ControlNet architecture featuring dual-branch control connectors for generation control.
contribution: Achieves impressive texture realism, visual vividness, and temporal consistency on synthetic and real-world benchmarks as well as AIGC videos.

problem: Long-context LLM decoding is bottlenecked by the expanding key-value cache, which grows linearly with sequence length.
approach: LycheeDecode partitions attention heads into retrieval heads (identifying crucial tokens) and sparse heads (reusing them), using a hardware-efficient top-k selection strategy.
contribution: Demonstrates comparable generative quality to full-attention baseline with up to 2.7x speedup at 128K context length across LongBench and RULER benchmarks.

problem: Brain-to-image decoding through fMRI typically relies on intermediate feature spaces, obscuring how brain signals shape generation.
approach: NeuroAdapter directly conditions a diffusion model on brain representations, bypassing intermediate feature spaces, with an interpretability framework probing cross-attention across denoising steps.
contribution: Provides competitive visual reconstruction quality on fMRI datasets with greater transparency into how different cortical areas influence generation.

problem: Fine-tuning LLMs with new data can inadvertently introduce unsafe behaviors or degrade safety alignment.
approach: GradShield computes a Finetuning Implicit Harmfulness Score for each data point and removes harmful samples before fine-tuning to preserve alignment.
contribution: Maintains Attack Success Rate under 6% while preserving utility performance across multiple fine-tuning tasks.

problem: LLM-based agents face high latency and inference costs that limit real-world deployment and user experience.
approach: DSP uses asynchronous online reinforcement learning to dynamically balance latency and cost without offline training, allowing user control over the acceleration-cost tradeoff.
contribution: Achieves comparable efficiency to the fastest lossless acceleration method while reducing total cost by 30% and unnecessary cost up to 60%.

problem: Knowledge distillation lacks theoretical understanding of how soft probabilistic outputs affect student convergence and generalization.
approach: The paper analyzes SGD convergence with Bayesian teachers that provide Bayes Class Probabilities, showing variance reduction and improved generalization bounds.
contribution: Students distilled from Bayesian teachers achieve up to 4.27% higher accuracies and exhibit 30% less noise in convergence compared to deterministic teachers.

problem: Logic optimization for chip design relies on expensive GNN-based pruning that is slow and hard to interpret.
approach: HIS learns a hierarchical tree structure to represent symbolic functions, trained with RL to optimize a Transformer for symbolic token generation that identifies ineffective subgraphs.
contribution: Outperforms previous state-of-the-art approaches in efficiency and optimization performance on two widely used circuit benchmarks.

problem: Fixed N:M sparsity in neural networks limits flexibility in adapting pruning to varying weight importance across layers.
approach: FlexHiNM-GP adaptively partitions layers into dense, vector-pruned, and N:M sparse regions with iterative channel-rearrangement (Gyro-Permutation) and differentiable Hard Concrete masking.
contribution: Consistently surpasses structured baselines and approaches unstructured pruning performance on vision and language benchmarks.

problem: Computing optimal transport maps requires numerical integration or adversarial training, which is computationally expensive.
approach: The method uses the Hamilton-Jacobi equation and characteristics method to derive closed-form bidirectional transport maps trained via a pure minimization framework.
contribution: Establishes a principled and versatile tool for optimal transport with provable optimality, demonstrating accuracy, scalability, and efficiency.

problem: Multimodal LLMs remain vulnerable to adversarial visual inputs despite existing safety defenses.
approach: GuardAlign combines optimal-transport-enhanced safety detection (measuring distribution distances) with cross-modal attentive calibration to strengthen safety signals during generation.
contribution: Reduces unsafe response rates by up to 39% on SPA-VL while improving utility (VQAv2 from 78.51% to 79.21%).

problem: Uncertainty estimation on resource-constrained microcontrollers is impractical because existing methods require multiple inference passes.
approach: SNAP-UQ predicts next activations from low-rank projections using tiny int8 heads, computing standardized prediction error as depth-wise surprisal signals aggregated into an uncertainty score.
contribution: Reduces flash and latency by 40-60% and 25-35% respectively compared to early-exit and ensemble baselines while maintaining AUROC ≈ 0.9 failure detection.

problem: Existing hallucination benchmarks for MLLMs use oversimplified tasks and fail to assess fine-grained visual perception.
approach: FREAK proposes fine-grained photorealistic images with counter-commonsense edits and evaluates hallucination via CoT prompting techniques on a controlled subset.
contribution: Reveals severe hallucination issues in SOTA models regarding fine-grained visual perception with critical insights on hallucination patterns.

problem: Solving inverse problems with diffusion models requires careful tuning or suffers from local optima and noise overfitting.
approach: NA-NHMC performs posterior sampling by treating reverse diffusion as a deterministic mapping from noise to images, enabling solution space exploration while keeping proposals on the learned manifold.
contribution: Achieves superior reconstruction quality across four linear and three nonlinear inverse problems, significantly outperforming recent state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Traditional gradient descent requires unrealistically large learning rates to escape saddle points during fine-tuning.
approach: The paper introduces steepest mirror flows as a theoretical framework showing that steeper descent facilitates saddle-point escape and feature learning better than gradient descent.
contribution: Explains why Adam and AdamW outperform SGD in fine-tuning through saddle-point escape and feature learning mechanisms.

problem: Deep neural networks do not align well with human visual behavior, exhibiting poor error consistency and weak shape bias.
approach: The method demonstrates that low-pass filtering (via image blurring at test-time) removes high-frequency information and improves behavioral alignment with human visual perception.
contribution: Halves the alignment gap between DNNs and human observers by blurring images at test-time, achieving state-of-the-art model-vs-human score.

problem: Watermarking verification in diffusion models requires slow, error-prone inversion that limits practical deployment.
approach: FARI proposes fast one-step inversion paired with lightweight adversarial LoRA fine-tuning, exploiting the lower curvature of inversion trajectories for efficient watermark extraction.
contribution: Surpasses 50-step DDIM inversion in both speed and robustness with ~20 minutes of fine-tuning on a single GPU.

problem: Evaluating multi-turn instruction-based image editing is unreliable because benchmarks lack paired references or rely only on VLMs.
approach: EdiVal-Agent decomposes images into objects, synthesizes diverse editing instructions, and measures instruction-following and content-consistency via object-centric metrics.
contribution: Enables automated fine-grained evaluation of multi-turn editing with object-centric metrics on a new video benchmark for category splitting.

problem: Detecting training data contamination in LLMs is difficult because it is hard to distinguish memorization from generalization.
approach: CoDeC measures how in-context learning affects model performance to distinguish memorized data from unseen datasets, producing model- and dataset-agnostic contamination scores.
contribution: Produces interpretable contamination scores that clearly separate seen and unseen datasets with strong evidence of memorization in open-weight models.

problem: Scaling laws for generative evaluations like math problem-solving remain underexplored, limiting prediction of model capabilities.
approach: Three pretraining scaling laws are proposed for fitting pass-at-k on generative evaluations, differing in covariates: compute, parameters-tokens, and log-likelihoods of solutions.
contribution: Identifies that generative evaluations introduce hyperparameters acting as control levers for scaling behavior, with the gold reference likelihood law uniquely stable across 5 orders.

problem: Predicting downstream LLM task performance from scaling laws is unreliable, limiting extrapolation of model capabilities.
approach: A two-parameter scaling law directly models downstream accuracy from training budget, validated on models up to 17B parameters trained on up to 350B tokens.
contribution: Accurately describes downstream accuracy scaling for fixed token-to-parameter ratio and enables extrapolation with up to 6.7x larger training budget.

problem: LLMs with persistent memory lack mechanisms to control information flow based on context, risking inappropriate disclosure.
approach: CIMemories uses synthetic user profiles with 100+ attributes and task contexts to evaluate whether LLMs control information flow appropriately across different scenarios.
contribution: Reveals frontier models exhibit 14%-69% attribute-level violations, highlighting critical gaps in integrity-aware memory systems.

problem: Fixed video classification taxonomies cannot accommodate emerging category distinctions without costly annotation and retraining.
approach: The method leverages latent compositional structure of video classifiers to expose fine-grained distinctions without additional data, enhanced by low-shot fine-tuning.
contribution: Substantially outperforms vision-language baselines on category splitting while preserving accuracy on the rest of the taxonomy.

problem: Existing copula models struggle to scale and represent multimodal dependencies in high-dimensional data.
approach: Diffusion and flow-based copulas model dependencies by learning to remember forgotten inter-variable dependencies, supporting both density estimation and efficient sampling.
contribution: Demonstrates superior performance over state-of-the-art copula approaches in modelling complex and high-dimensional dependencies.

problem: Generating realistic human geometry with fine clothing details and accurate body interactions at scale is computationally inefficient.
approach: A two-stage generative framework encodes geometry distributions as 2D feature maps using flow matching, then trains a flow model on the latent space with SMPL domain refinement.
contribution: Achieves 57% improvement in geometry quality for pose-conditioned avatar generation and novel pose synthesis over existing methods.

problem: Large Vision-Language Models suffer from hallucinations that degrade performance on vision-language tasks.
approach: Dynamic Multimodal Activation Steering constructs a semantic-based truthfulness steering vector database and computes visual perception vectors, applied to influential attention heads.
contribution: Significantly enhances model performance and outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in hallucination mitigation across multiple models and datasets.

problem: Identifying promising reasoning traces early is difficult, wasting computation on unproductive paths during inference-time scaling.
approach: Latent-trajectory signals characterize temporal evolution of internal representations during reasoning, enabling early selection of promising candidates during generation.
contribution: Reduces token usage by up to 70% while preserving and improving accuracy by 2.6% on average compared to majority voting.

problem: Evaluating LLMs on realistic software development tasks with long code context remains a gap in current benchmarks.
approach: SwingArena pairs LLMs as patch submitters and reviewers in CI pipelines, with a retrieval-augmented code generation module handling long-context challenges.
contribution: Presents a scalable methodology for evaluating LLMs in realistic CI-driven software development with over 400 real-world GitHub issues.

problem: Offline RL must balance preventing out-of-distribution actions with learning expressive multimodal policies.
approach: ReFORM learns a behavior-cloning flow with bounded source distribution, then optimizes a reflected flow generating bounded noise while keeping the support.
contribution: Dominates all baselines on 40 OGBench tasks with constant hyperparameters, maintaining strong performance across datasets of varying quality.

problem: Deep learning for electronic-structure Hamiltonian prediction struggles to generalize across diverse materials.
approach: NextHAM introduces zeroth-step Hamiltonians as descriptors, uses a Transformer with E(3)-symmetry, and proposes training objectives for accuracy in both real and reciprocal space.
contribution: Demonstrates improved generalization on Materials-HAM-SOC, a dataset of 17,000 materials spanning 60+ elements with spin-orbit coupling effects.

problem: Novel view synthesis from sparse RGB fails under rapid camera motion, and event-based methods require per-scene optimization.
approach: EA3D jointly leverages event streams and RGB imagery via an EA-Renderer that fuses appearance with event-based geometry, conditioned to a 3D-informed diffusion model.
contribution: Consistently outperforms optimization-based and generalizable baselines on both real-world and synthetic event data with superior fidelity.

problem: SVG understanding, editing, and generation remain fragmented tasks with limited dataset and method transferability.
approach: InternSVG leverages MLLMs with SVG-specific tokens and two-stage training progressing from static SVGs to animations, trained on the large SAgoge dataset.
contribution: Achieves substantial gains and consistently outperforms leading open and proprietary counterparts on SVG understanding, editing, and generation.

problem: Multimodal LLMs struggle to understand real-world scenarios from synchronized audio-visual input.
approach: WorldSense designs omni-modal evaluation tasks requiring audio and video synergies across 1,662 videos in 8 domains with 3,172 multi-choice QA pairs.
contribution: Demonstrates that existing models achieve only 65.1% best accuracy on real-world omni-modal understanding tasks across 1,662 audio-visual videos.

problem: Graph neural networks lack large-scale datasets that capture spatial multi-edges and complex geometric structures.
approach: Poly2Graph automates mapping 1-D Hamiltonians to spectral graphs, generating HSG-12M containing 11.6M static and 5.1M dynamic spatial multigraphs.
contribution: Introduces HSG-12M with 11.6M static and 5.1M dynamic spatial multigraphs, the first large-scale dataset of spatial multigraphs for graph learning.

problem: The expressiveness of transformers and their ability to represent formal languages remains theoretically unexplored.
approach: The paper proves that transformers can represent formal languages more succinctly than finite automata and LTL formulas via a succinctness measure.
contribution: Proves that transformers are EXPSPACE-complete in expressive power, substantially surpassing finite automata and LTL formulas.

problem: Language models struggle with table understanding due to structured data complexity and lack of semantic context.
approach: TableMaster extracts and verbalizes table content with semantic context and introduces adaptive reasoning that flexibly adjusts between textual and symbolic reasoning.
contribution: Achieves 78.13% accuracy on WikiTQ using GPT-4o-mini, surpassing existing baselines for table understanding.
